placeslab.howNote.beam: Two clicks: the two ends of the beam. Clicks snap to axes, columns and corners within 12 px.
placeslab.howNote.column: One click: the column's centre. The section is square. Clicks snap to axes, columns and corners within 12 px.
placeslab.howNote.footing: One click on a column: the footing is centred under it, its top at the column's base. Elsewhere: its top at the level. IfcFooting PAD_FOOTING.
placeslab.howNote.grid_axis: Two clicks in a plan: the axis' start and end (snapped to the axes and their crossings; Shift: along x or y). Its name follows those of its direction (1, 2, 3… or A, B, C…). Esc cancels.
placeslab.howNote.opening: Two clicks on a wall (its two sides, with the height and sill) or on a slab (two opposite corners). It goes through the element and follows it. Refused outside the element or over another opening.
placeslab.howNote.raft: Click the corners; the first corner or Enter closes. The raft's top is flush with the lowest level. IfcSlab BASESLAB.
placeslab.howNote.slab: Two clicks: two opposite corners. The slab's top is flush with level {above}. Clicks snap to axes, columns and corners within 12 px.
placeslab.howNote.sleeve: One click on a wall or a slab: a round sleeve goes through it (a 32-sided polygon). In a wall, centred on its height.
placeslab.howNote.strip_footing: One click on a wall: the footing runs under the whole wall, its top at the wall's base. Elsewhere: two clicks, its two ends. IfcFooting STRIP_FOOTING.
placeslab.howNote.wall: Two clicks: the two ends of the wall's axis. Clicks snap to axes, columns and corners within 12 px.

settings.gpuCull: Culling copies on the graphics card: with the WebGPU renderer only (WebGL2 has no compute shaders).

settings.kept: Memory per model, simplified far parts and GPU culling: kept in the file for the desktop app, no effect here.
settings.linkDetailNote: Curves as triangles, and openings that take nothing away: Exact reads as before (none of it). A change converts each linked file again at its next load or Reload. Meshes given by the file stay as they are.
settings.linkGpuNote: The linked files' detail fits in this memory: past it, the farthest or out of view are drawn simplified, and their detail comes back as you get near.
settings.linkMaxDeg: Angle per chord (degrees; under 20: no edge along a cylinder)
settings.moving.0Note: Draw everything: the complete picture while the view moves too, as long as a frame takes under 100 ms. Above that, moving frames are kept near 60 ms (the largest elements first) and the complete picture comes as soon as the view stops.
settings.movingNote: While orbiting, the elements largest on screen first, as many as the frame rate allows; the rest as outlines, completed when the view stops.
settings.name: Name
settings.openApp: Open Bimble in an app window (Chromium)
settings.openAppNote: At the next “bimble-ccore open”: Chromium or Chrome in its own window, with its own profile and, on Linux, the flags that give WebGPU (--use-angle=vulkan --enable-features=Vulkan --enable-unsafe-webgpu). Without Chromium, the usual browser.
settings.optimNote: Each setting has an exact value: lines, nothing left out, back faces drawn, the picture completed on screen. Back faces are exact only for closed solids: off by default.
settings.proxiesNote: A far part is drawn as a simplified stand-in when it differs by less than 1 pixel when still, 3 pixels while moving; never for a selected, hidden or cut element. Measuring and snapping use the real geometry.
settings.refill: Complete the picture offscreen after a move
settings.rendererNote: WebGPU draws with the graphics card when the browser gives one; else WebGL2, and the Performance panel says why.

settings.visibleNote: A still picture leaves out what the previous picture from the same viewpoint shows hidden behind something else (the inside behind facades and slabs): fewer triangles, the same picture. Never in a plan or a section; a section box opens the inside. Off by default until it is verified on large projects of links.
